title: NRO/NGA Senate and GAO audit over carryover funds

tellings.quote: they underwent a uh, Senate and GAO audit for enormous uh, misappropriation of funds, specifically carryover funds, back in 1994, 1995, uh, in the realm of $3.2 billion or so.

plain: In 1994 and 1995, two US spy agencies were audited by the Senate and by the GAO, the auditing office that works for Congress, over what a researcher who goes by UAPGerb calls an "enormous" misuse of funds. The agencies were the NRO, which runs America's spy satellites, and the NGA, which handles maps and imagery. UAPGerb tells Michels the money was "carryover funds," meaning money left unspent and rolled into later years, "in the realm of $3.2 billion or so." He gives no source, though he draws on David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower, and he raises it to suggest how large sums could build up out of view to pay for a hidden UFO programme.
